newsitem.title: GERMANY: BMW overtakes Daimler in share race.
newsitem.headline: BMW overtakes Daimler in share race.

text.p: German car shares sped ahead in a pre-Easter share market race on Thursday, with BMW finally pipping Daimler-Benz AG at the post.

German car shares were racing after strong 1996 profit reports released this week, the more dramatic of which came on Wednesday as Daimler reported a firm recovery from 1995's unprecedented losses and vowed to reinstate its dividend.

But BMW ended Thursday's floor trade with gains of 3.5 percent, or 45 marks, at 1,350 marks while Daimler, whose shares have a nominal value of five marks compared with BMW's 50, managed an advance of just 1.3 percent to 133.40 marks.
The car sector overall rose six times faster than the broader maker, with the DAX 100 auto sector index rising 1.8 percent compared with the DAX's 0.3 percent advance.
BMW had on Tuesday reported one of its most successful years ever, with sales growth of 13.3 percent, although it warned that this pace would be unlikely to hold this year.
Lehman Brothers on Thursday raised its target price for BMW to 1,600 marks, after the stock bypassed its former target of 1,300.
Hot on BMW's heels, and unexpectedly, Daimler reported net profits of 2.8 billion marks for 1996, up from a 5.7 billion mark loss in 1995 and said it would pay a dividend of 1.10 marks per share
"I wouldn't be surprised if Daimler only released those numbers to catch up with BMW," said a Munich trader.
"The numbers were really much better than expected. They had all the more impact because nobody was expecting them until next month."
Thursday's advance bring BMW's share price advance this week to 13.6 percent and Daimler's to 5.6 percent.
